name: 01-headless-replacement
title: S1 · Headless text-only turn after a conversation-only rewind
sub: Real dist/cli.js bundles, keyboard in tmux, loopback model, real read_file/write_file. MARK_A, MARK_B (no edit) → MARK_C edits state.txt BASELINE→OLD_EDIT → Esc Esc → Restore conversation only on MARK_C (checkpoint #2 retained) → qwen --resume <id> -p "MARK_D …" → interactive --resume, rewind selector on MARK_D.

panels.head: main @ 1e1c4a4: MARK_D was minted ordinal 2 (the retained checkpoint's identity), so the text-only turn offers a code restore
main @ 1e1c4a4: choosing "Restore code only" reverts an edit this turn never made
main + PR 13729 (head 79a6d01, trial merge): MARK_D was minted ordinal 3, no file restore is offered, and the file is untouched

note: Control on both arms, same session: a real edit turn (MARK_E, →CTRL_EDIT) still offers and performs "Restore code only" (Restored 1 file(s).).

name: 02-interactive-resume
title: S2 / S4 · Interactive --resume path (the Ink seed computeResumedPromptCountSeed)
sub: After the conversation-only rewind, resume interactively, send a text-only MARK_D, then an edit MARK_E (OLD_EDIT→NEW_EDIT), then Esc Esc → MARK_D → Restore code only. Expected: state.txt back to OLD_EDIT (MARK_D's starting state).

panels.head: S2 · main @ 1e1c4a4: MARK_D re-minted ordinal 2 → two checkpoints share one identity → restore refused
S2 · main + PR 13729 (head 79a6d01, trial merge): MARK_D minted ordinal 3 → restore works
S4 (first turn edits; rewind removes every user turn) · main @ 1e1c4a4: MARK_D re-minted ordinal 0 → refused
S4 · main + PR 13729 (head 79a6d01, trial merge): MARK_D minted ordinal 1 → restore works

name: 04-acp-rewind
title: ACP rewind after a TUI conversation-only rewind (pre-existing position offset)
sub: Same TUI fixture as S1, then --acp stdio: session/load, prompts, and the rewind control the daemon HTTP route forwards (it requires promptId).

note: ACP resolves promptId → snapshots.findIndex() position → turn index. The TUI conversation-only rewind keeps the target turn's checkpoint, so every later position is shifted by one. Row 3 shows this already on main. The PR removes the silent stale-file restore for F; F then lands on the same one-turn-late cut every later turn already had. Not a regression from this diff; #13737 says ACP will "resolve recorded boundaries independently of snapshot indexes" (not run here).
